newsitem.title: USA: Glickman sees need for new livestock disaster plan.
newsitem.headline: Glickman sees need for new livestock disaster plan.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said there needed to be an urgent dialogue between the U.S. Department of Agriculture and Congress about emergency livestock assistance as the government's ability to respond is rapidly dwindling.

"Lately we have seen an increase in extreme weather conditions and it has taken its toll on our grain reserve, which is our only source for livestock assistance in disaster," Glickman said at the National Cattlemen's Beef Association's annual convention here.

"We do need a permanent system to help cattle ranchers in crisis and working with Congress to figure it out now rather than wait until disaster strikes, the grain reserve is gone and we are powerless to respond," he said.
"If extreme weather patterns continue, that is a position we could be in in a year or two. The time for dialogue is now," Glickman said.

He noted that at the beginning of 1996 there were 45 million bushels of government-owned feedgrain. Since then 15 million had been sold following a drought in the Southwest and more would be sold for disaster relief in the Dakotas and Northerns Plains.
"In less than a year we have gone through well over a third of our grain reserves," he said.
